about: What the port of Up Your Arsenal does differently from the PS2 game. Read by the port's build (port/cmake/Differences.cmake: the Game fixes settings). docs/port/SETTINGS.md section 8 says how to add an entry.

differences.name: Wide-screen effects
differences.original: A moby near the side of a picture wider than 4:3 counts as out of view for its effects.
differences.port: MobyProc's drawn test runs against the wider picture, as Going Commando's: a moby drawn makes its effects, as it would on a wider console picture. Off, it runs against the 4:3 view, and the effects of mobys near the sides are missing.

differences.name: Wide-screen scenery
differences.original: The draw callbacks cull what they send against the 4:3 view.
differences.port: Each draw callback list runs with the view tests opened as far as the picture is wider. Off, they run against the 4:3 view, and what they draw is missing near the sides.

differences.name: Wider pictures
differences.original: A 4:3 picture, or the game's own 16:9 option, which narrows the vertical view and leaves the television to stretch it.
differences.port: A wider picture keeps the game's vertical field of view and shows more of the world to the sides. The game's 16:9 option has no meaning in a window, and the port keeps it off; the title Options' 16:9 row is the port's Video page instead.
